ischemic epithelial cells undergo a rapid and selective degradation of E-caddherin with a concomitant loss of AJ protein complexes.

ischemia-induced disruption of intercelluar junctions and loss apical-basolar polarity in epithelial cells is associated with the selective degradation of E-caddherin and the dissolution of E-caddhern-catenin complexes, and that the reassembly AJ after ischemia may require the recombination of newly-synthesized and sorted E-caddherins with preexisting catenins that are redistributed intracellularly.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of ischemic epithelial injury and with the reassembly of epithelial cells after ATP depletion.
understanding the mechanisms by which ischemia disrupts the normal function and structure of the AJ, and how the AJ is reconstituted after ischemia.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying the disruption and reassembly of the epithelial AJ during ischemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ischemic epithelial cells have a disrupted adherens junction (i.e., E-cadherins and catenins are degraded and dissociated) and that the reestablishment of the adherens (and other) junctions requires a novel mechanism for the reassembly of these proteins.
ATP depletion results in the selective degradation of E-caddherin and disruption of E-cad-catenin complexes.
the loss of E-caddherin and its catenins is a key step for the disruption of the AJ in ischemic epithelial cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of E-caddherin and catenins from the plasma membrane, and the disruption of E-cad/catenin complex assembly are critical components in the ischemic cell phenotype.
the ischemic epithelium is characterized by a loss of cell-cell adhesions and the dissolution of the AJ.
ischemic epithelial cells undergo a rapid degradation of E cadherin with subsequent disruption of the AJ.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the loss of E-caddherin and the disruption of AJ are important steps in the ischemic epithelia phenotype, which is characterized by loss of cell-cell adhesion, disruption of apical-basal polarity, and the development of a leaky epithelial barrier.

the ischemic epithelium is a dynamic system in which the AJ is rapidly disassembled by a protease that functions under conditions of low ATP and low intracellular calcium, and then reassembled in a novel fashion after ATP depletion is relieved.
the ischemic epithelium is not a simple extension of the normal epithelium, but rather is a unique cell population with distinct properties and functions.
